title: 198.5 Points, and the 9–0 Team Is Now No. 2
dek: Connor & Kunal post the top score of the season and take over the power rankings, Peyton wins again anyway, and Mike's playoff odds jump to 94%.

sections.head: The lead
body: Got New Legs scored **198.5 points** on Sunday. That is the best single week anyone has put up this season, and it came at Trey's expense: 198.5 to 113.4, an 85.1-point beating. Trey scored a perfectly respectable number and was never in it.

It also settled an argument this column has been having with itself for weeks. Connor & Kunal are now No. 1 in the power rankings, with an .838 all-play mark and a 146.1 average over the last three weeks. The models agree: they carry a 48.5% chance at the title, about double anyone else's.

sections.head: Meanwhile, at 9–0
body: Peyton just keeps winning. The Loose Stools beat Chris & Miguel 134.5 to 121.1, stayed the league's only unbeaten team, clinched the division, and got bumped to No. 2 in the power rankings for their trouble. Peyton now leads the series with Bad JuJu 11–8.
The luck chart still has notes. Peyton has scored like a 6.9-win team and owns nine. Title odds sit at 25%, half of Connor & Kunal's. Nobody in the Stools' locker room is reading that column.

sections.head: Around the league
body: Kevin brought up the rear with 63.3 and lost to John 114.0 to 63.3, a 50.8-point margin. He left 41.1 points on the bench, which is the bench blunder of the week and still wouldn't have caught John. Due For A Win remains, technically, due. John now leads that series 17–8.

The upset belonged to Andrew & Nick, who knocked off Michael 107.8 to 94.6 despite being rated 59 Elo points lower. Mike handled Nathan 129.1 to 100.1, and Mack beat Dustin 99.4 to 80.0, though Dustin still leads that series 13–5.

sections.head: Power shifts
body: Mike climbed to No. 3 and Chris & Miguel slid to No. 4. John jumped two spots to No. 8, Trey fell to No. 9, and Kevin hit the floor at No. 12, averaging 67.6 over his last three.

Mack is 7–2 and ranked fifth, which tells you most of what you need to know. His all-play mark is .495 and he's won about 2.5 more games than his scoring deserves, the most in the league. Nathan is the mirror image: 3–6, scoring like a 4.8-win team.

sections.head: The playoff picture
body: Connor & Kunal and Peyton are in, and Mack is at 99.6%. The big mover is Mike, from 76% to 94% with the win over Nathan. Chris & Miguel dipped slightly to 93%.
The sixth spot is Trey's for now at 44% and 4–5, with Nathan at 32%. Michael took the week's worst hit, from 25% to 10%, and Kevin fell from 15% to 6%. John went the other way, from 4% to 11%.

sections.head: Game of the Week
body: Dustin vs. Trey. Dustin is 2–7 and projected for 121.4, Trey is projected for 114.9, and Dustin is a 58% favorite. The result moves the two teams' playoff odds by a combined 40 points. Trey leads the all-time series 9–6.
Nathan vs. Chris & Miguel carries almost as much, also 40 points, with Nathan a 58% favorite. And the Stools' shot at 10–0 comes against John, in a series tied 8–8–1. Peyton is a 59% favorite.

groupme: Week 9 is in. Connor & Kunal dropped 198.5 on Trey, the best score of the season, and took over No. 1 in the power rankings from the 9–0 Stools. Mike's playoff odds jumped from 76% to 94%. Next up: Dustin vs. Trey, with 40 points of playoff odds on the line, and Peyton chasing 10–0 against John in a series tied 8–8–1.
